title: When a bell alert or a member pop-up cannot be made, nobody ever finds out
what: About 25 places in the newer server rules catch any error while making a bell alert, a member pop-up, the 'credits low' or 'members used this month's AI answers' alert, or while marking an alert as done. Each one only writes a warning line into the database log and carries on. HQ reads that log for direct-read lines only, never these warnings. The check 'may this person see this alert' also turns any error into 'no' without writing anything. So a broken alert rule makes alerts silently go missing (or stay on the bell after the thing is done) for every gym until someone happens to notice.
expected: The member's action still saves, but each failed alert is counted somewhere HQ looks, and a rising count raises a warning.
how_often: only when an alert rule breaks, then for every gym
fix_line: Write each failed alert to a small failures table and show its count on HQ

title: An unused server door for counting web page visitors' AI questions is still open
what: The AI questions change added a separate way to charge a gym's credits for a web page visitor's question. Nothing calls it: the web page AI helper charges through its own chat step instead. The unused door is still open to the public app key (it needs our web server's signature), so it is extra code to keep safe and in step with the real rule, for no use.
expected: Code nothing uses is removed, or closed to the public key until it is needed.
fix_line: Remove the unused visitor door, or take away the public key's access to it

title: The 'today' rule is typed out by hand about 30 times, and one daily limit uses a different day
what: A shared rule for 'today in India' exists, yet these 36 change files write the India day out by hand about 30 times. One limit uses neither: the direct-read record's 2,000-a-day cap counts a UTC day, which starts at 5:30 am in India, while every other daily limit counts an India day.
expected: Every daily rule uses the one shared India-day rule.
fix_line: Use the shared India-day rule everywhere, including the direct-read cap
